// diagnostic

E1103

`.detach()` called on a task that had a sendability error (E1102) at spawn.

What

`.detach()` called on a task that had a sendability error (E1102) at spawn.

Why

A detached task runs unsupervised and may outlive the caller; a task that already has sendability problems is doubly unsafe to detach.

Fix

Fix the E1102 error at the spawn site first; once the task only holds owned data, `.detach()` is safe.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E1103: tests/ui/task_detach_unsound.stderr.

Error [E0120]: `greet` was not moved here, so it cannot be captured by a spawned task
  --> tests/ui/task_detach_unsound.jet:5:15
    |
  5 |     t :: task greet
    |               ^^^^^
 Why: this function can access the parameter, but it does not own the value; capture requires the move marker `^`
 Fix: make the parameter owned with the move marker `^`: `greet: ^fn()`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0120

Error [E1102]: this task returns `fn()`, which isn't sendable
  --> tests/ui/task_detach_unsound.jet:5:15
    |
  5 |     t :: task greet
    |               ^^^^^
 Why: the closure holds state that cannot cross this boundary; tasks and channels move owned values between threads
 Fix: give the task plain owned data, or rebuild the value as an owned copy before spawning
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1102

Error [E1103]: can't detach task `t` — it captured a value that can't cross a thread boundary
  --> tests/ui/task_detach_unsound.jet:6:7
    |
  6 |     t.detach()
    |       ^^^^^^
 Why: a detached task runs unsupervised; it must only hold values it owns cleanly
 Fix: fix the E1102 error at the spawn site first, then `.detach()` is safe
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1103
